text:
marco: Quick thread on slot reclamation / compaction handshake ideas after the perf run. TL;DR: avoid blind sweeps, prefer an explicit refund/ack handshake.
anya: +1. Blind sweeps cause spikes and double-free races with admission credits.
lee: Observed a 300ms tail when batcher reclaimed slots synchronously during high churn.
marco: Proposal sketch: three pieces - passive occupancy stream, reclaim request from scheduler, reclaim ACK with credits returned.
julia: Can you sketch wire?
marco: Sure. Minimal proto:```text
GET /batcher/state -> {lane_id, slots_used, slots_free, head_gap}
POST /batcher/reclaim -> {lane_id, target_free, mode:async|sync} -> returns job_id
POST /batcher/reclaim/ack -> {job_id, freed_slots}
POST /scheduler/credits/apply -> {token, amount}
```
anya: Important: `reclaim` must be idempotent and lease-protected. If scheduler retries, batcher should return same job_id.
lee: Also add a `lease_token` field so reclaim is scoped to scheduler-run. Prevents cross-host double-reclaim.
marco: Good call. Add `lease_token` and a `deadline_ms`.
marco: Another idea: shaping signal vs reclaim. Shaping = ask batcher to coalesce small entries before doing expensive compaction. Reclaim = guaranteed free-up.
julia: Shaping is lower risk. Batcher can respond with `shaped:true|false` quickly.
anya: How do we avoid oscillation? Scheduler might request reclaim then immediately schedule new work into freed slots.
lee: Use a short grace window: batcher holds freed slots for X ms and reports them as "reserved_for_scheduler" in state stream. Scheduler must consume reserved slots before they go back to general pool.
marco: That ties into credits: when reclaim completes we emit a `credits.returned` event with the same token scheduler used to allocate. Scheduler can then reuse that token to admit new requests.
julia: What about cross-batcher compaction ordering? If multiple batchers host a lane, we need consistent hole semantics.
anya: Keep placement invariant inside batcher. Scheduler coordinates by lane_owner id. Only lane_owner can trigger reclaim on that lane. If ownership moves, the lease_token becomes invalid.
lee: Rollout plan: (1) export lightweight occupancy stream (every 100-250ms) with `head_gap` metric, (2) implement shaping endpoint, (3) add reclaim RPC with async ack, (4) integrate credit return in scheduler.
marco: Perf tests to run: high-churn small-requests, compaction-heavy traces, multi-host ownership transfer. Measure p99 tail and credit latency.
julia: Devops-bot: canary deploy scheduled: batcher-reclaim-v1 -> canary 5% eu-west at 02:00 UTC.
devops-bot: deploy-queued: healthchecks will run for 20m.
anya: Edge case: what if reclaim job fails mid-work? Batcher should report a partial `freed_slots` and keep a retryable marker. Scheduler should not assume full amount.
lee: And add `approx_freed_tokens` so scheduler can plan.
marco: Action items: marco -> draft RFC with proto + failure modes; anya -> add occupancy stream; lee -> perf harness scenarios; julia -> canary checklist. I'll ping with RFC link.
anya: +1 from me. Let's be conservative with aggressive reclaim until we see perf numbers.
julia: Thanks all. I'll add a small note to the release notes about new endpoints. :white_check_mark:
